title: Stride synchronous throughput sweep for TP/PP multi-GPU inference
creator: Anika Rao
description: Objective: Build a reproducible sweep to measure steady-state and burst throughput across tensor- and pipeline-parallel topologies. The sweep ("stride synchronous") will exercise varying micro-batch strides, KV cache warmup strategies, and inter-node NVLink/PCIe contention scenarios to quantify tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, and regression sensitivity when scaling from 1 to 16 GPUs. Deliverables: test harness, perf dashboards, automated regression alerts, and a recommendations doc for runtime scheduler defaults.
goals: Measure sustainable tokens/sec across TP/PP configurations for model families (Llama2-13B, Llama2-70B, custom quantized variant)
Track p95/p99 and steady-state variance to inform SLA targets
Detect regressions by integrating a baseline fingerprint and weekly scheduled runs
Characterize warmup costs with prefix caching enabled vs disabled
environment: Nodes: 4x nodes (each: 4x A100-80GB with NVLink full mesh)
Network: 100GbE fabric + NVLink intra-node; tests also run with artificially capped PCIe paths
Software: runtime-1.22-rc, kernel selection heuristics enabled, custom quantization profiles
tests: steady_state_stride: fixed stride sizes [1,2,4,8] with continuous stream until 2M tokens
microburst_sweep: 100 concurrent short requests to measure transient token throughput
kv_warmup_vs_cold: compare cold starts vs warmed KV cache profiles
node_scaling: 1->16 GPUs increasing TP/PP slices to find scaling knee
degraded_link: simulate a single NVLink failure and observe graceful degradation
metrics: steady_state_variance (coefficient of variation over sliding 5m windows)
acceptance_criteria: Automated job runs reproducibly produce tokens/sec within +/-10% of baseline for 3 consecutive runs
Regression detector integration posts alerts when tokens/sec drops >12% or p95 increases >20% compared to baseline
Dashboard panels (per-model, per-topology) exist with historic comparison and per-GPU breakdown
Run artifacts (raw logs, perf counters, flamegraphs, golden traces) are stored in S3 for 90 days
steps: Create param file generator for stride/microbatch combinations
Bootstrap cluster images with runtime-1.22-rc and monitoring agents
Implement KV cache priming helper and deterministic warmup corpus
Run baseline sweep (L2-13B FP16) and record fingerprint
Add nightly CI job that runs lightweight subset and invokes regression detector

risks_and_tradeoffs: Running full 16-GPU sweeps is costly — we will gate full runs behind a successful small-scale regression check
Aggressive caching may mask real cold-start regressions; we keep both warm and cold measurements
Synthetic workloads may not capture all customer patterns; we'll collect representative prompts from customers (anonymized) for a follow-up sweep
